The associated on-call work is included within the 10 PA job plan, and the post carries no neonatal on-call commitment. This is a varied whole-time post that combines hospital (medical) paediatrics with community child health. The hospital component includes five general paediatric hot weeks a year on the Highland Children’s Ward as consultant of the week, general paediatric outpatient clinics at Raigmore, and a quarterly visit to Caithness with clinics at Thurso and Wick. The community component includes locality clinics in Inverness, a travelling locality clinic outside Inverness with the travel job-planned, and a roughly monthly clinic at the Belford Hospital in Fort William, together with child protection medical assessments and case conferences, medical assessments for looked-after and adopted children, and a share of the weekday child protection rota. Outside the five hot weeks the timetable is arranged across four weekdays, leaving one day (currently Friday) clear of fixed sessions, so a compressed four-day week is possible for those who would prefer it; this would be settled at formal job planning. Clinical supervision of a paediatric trainee and undergraduate teaching form part of the post. Out-of-hours duties are on a non-resident consultant rota for general paediatric emergencies, approximately 1:10, with no neonatal on-call commitment.
